title: Cognitive Dissonance Theory: Core Concepts
text:
Cognitive dissonance theory, pioneered by Leon Festinger, describes the mental stress or discomfort experienced by an individual who holds two or more conflicting beliefs, values, or ideas. This psychological tension suggests that humans are intrinsically motivated to maintain internal consistency among their cognitions.

To alleviate this uncomfortable state, individuals are compelled to modify one or more of the dissonant elements. Modification can occur through changing attitudes (convincing oneself a belief is wrong), altering behavior (changing actions), or adding new consonant beliefs (rationalizing the inconsistency with external justifications). The magnitude of dissonance is proportional to the importance of the conflicting cognitions.
